summary: Suraaqa bin Maalik, still a non-Muslim at the time, pursued the Prophet during the Hijrah, and his horse's legs sank into the sand after the Prophet made du'aa.
Suraaqa pleads for his horse to be freed, the Prophet and Abu Bakr make du'aa, and Suraaqa then turns back the pursuers and becomes a defender of the Prophet.
notes: Several separate reports run together (Umayr bin Is'haaq, Abu Ma'bad Khuzaa'ee, Anas). The text ends mid-sentence with a cross-reference to the Hijrah chapter.

summary: Arbad bin Qais and Aamir bin Tufayl plot to kill the Prophet, Arbad is struck by lightning, and Aamir dies after developing a swelling on his throat.
notes: Quotes Qur'aan verses (Ra'd 8-13) within the text.

summary: At the Battle of Hunayn the Prophet threw earth or pebbles at the enemy, and they were defeated as if every tree and stone were chasing them.
notes: Two reports: Haarith bin Badal says earth was thrown, Amr bin Sufyaan says pebbles.

summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam relates that at Badr, after hearing a sound like stones falling on a platter, the Mushrikeen were defeated when the Prophet threw pebbles at them.
Hakeem bin Hizaam relates that the Prophet was instructed to throw a handful of pebbles at the Mushrikeen at Badr, and that Allaah then revealed Surah Anfaal verse 17.
Ibn Abbaas reports that at Badr the Prophet took pebbles from Ali and threw them into the enemy's faces, and that Allaah then revealed Surah Anfaal verse 17.
Yazeed bin Aamir Suwaa'ee reports that the Prophet threw a handful of soil at the enemy at Badr, after which the Mushrikeen complained of dust in their eyes.
notes: Yazeed bin Aamir is not in the approved list.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood recalls that the enemy looked very few in number at Badr, until a captured man revealed they were a thousand strong.
Sa'eed bin Jubayr describes the combined forces that marched on Madinah at Khandaq, and how Allaah sent a wind and angels against them so that they fled.
notes: Jibra'eel is named and brings the wind, but he is an angel, not a person, so he is left out. Banu Qurayzah and the other tribes are not persons.

summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that Banu Qurayzah broke their pact by joining the Mushrikeen, and that Allaah sent an army and wind that routed the Mushrikeen while Qurayzah stayed in their fortress.
notes: Ends with an ellipsis; the narration continues with the battle against Banu Qurayzah.

summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that during the Battle of Ahzaab the east wind was sent to assist the Prophet, because the north wind refused to travel by night.

Buraydah reports that a Mushrik who prayed for Muhammad's falsehood to be shown sank into the ground at Uhud, and Naafi bin Aasim reports that the man who wounded the Prophet's face was gored to death by a ram.
notes: Two reports in one item. Abdullaah bin Qami'ah may be the person in the approved list as ibn-qamia, but I did not match him to that id.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mughaffal recounts that at Hudaybiyyah thirty armed Quraysh youths were blinded by the Prophet's curse, were then released, and Surah Fath verse 24 was revealed.
Zaadhaan reports that when Ali was accused of lying, he challenged the accuser to a curse, and the man lost his sight before leaving the gathering.
notes: The accuser is unnamed.

summary: Ammaar reports the same incident, in which the man who accused Ali of lying was blinded by Ali's curse, and a second Zaadhaan account is included.
notes: Ammaar's report and a second Zaadhaan account run together. OCR is garbled near the join, so the wording of the second account is uncertain.

summary: Sa'eed bin Zaid prays that Arwa bint Uwais, who falsely claimed his land, be blinded if she is lying, and she falls into her well and dies; a flood then proves his claim.

people.name: Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam

notes: Several narrations are joined: Abdullaah bin Umar, Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam, and his childhood anecdote. The Prophet is quoted in Sa'eed's words (a hadith).

summary: Abu Utaaridi warns against reviling Ali or the Prophet's family, reporting that a man from Balhujaym who scoffed at Husayn bin Ali lost his sight.
notes: The Balhujaym man is unnamed.

summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts that Quraysh men who tried to seize the Prophet in the Masjidul Haraam were blinded, then had their sight restored by his du'aa after pleading by family ties, and that Surah Yaaseen verses were revealed.
notes: The Quraysh men are unnamed. The item ends with the Qur'aan verses quoted.

summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan recounts losing his eye while shielding the Prophet at Uhud, and the Prophet restored it so that it became the better and sharper of his two eyes.
notes: Two reports: Qataadah's own account and Mahmood bin Labeed's shorter report from him.

summary: Another narration confirms that the eye became the better and sharper of the two.
notes: Short addendum to n03540. Neither the narrator nor the Companion is named in the text, so no person is tagged.

summary: Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah reports that the Companions wanted to cut off Qataadah's dislodged eye, and the Prophet reset it with his palm so that Qataadah could no longer tell which eye had been wounded.
Ubaydah reports that the Prophet applied his saliva to Abu Dharr's injured eye at Uhud, and it became the better of his two eyes.
Rifaa'ah bin Raafi reports that the Prophet's saliva and du'aa removed the pain of an arrow in his eye at Badr, and Habeeb bin Fuwayk reports that the Prophet restored his father's sight with saliva.
notes: Two reports in one item. Habeeb's father is unnamed in the text.

summary: Sa'eed bin Ibraheem reports that the freed Roman woman Zinneera regained her sight after she rejected Laat and Uzza, and Anas reports from Ummu Haani that Abu Bakr had freed her and that her sight was restored.
notes: Two reports joined (Sa'eed bin Ibraheem; Anas from Ummu Haani). The Quraysh speakers are unnamed.

summary: Hishaam bin Aas recounts his mission, sent by Abu Bakr, to invite Heraclius to Islaam, the palace shaking at the takbeer, and Heraclius showing them pictures of the prophets and then of the Prophet.
notes: Long single account with OCR garbling. The prophets shown in the pictures are tagged as mentioned. Heraclius's interpreter is unnamed. The Prophet appears through his picture and Heraclius's remarks.

summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im recounts that Christians in a church showed him pictures of the Prophet and of Abu Bakr, and said that Abu Bakr would be the Khalifah after him.
notes: The Christians are unnamed.

summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im relates that a Christian told him there is no Nabi after the Prophet, and that the man following the Prophet in the picture is his Khalifah, which Jubayr confirmed was Abu Bakr.
notes: The Christian who speaks is unnamed.

summary: Scholars from the Ghassaan and Banu Qayn report that, as a reward for patience at Hims, Allaah shook the city with an earthquake when the Muslims called out Allaahu Akbar, and the Romans were humbled.
notes: The scholars are unnamed and the narration continues in the original.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar called out 'The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain!' during a sermon, and Saariyah's army heard it, turned to the mountain and were granted victory.
notes: The messenger who came from the army is unnamed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gives further accounts of Umar's call to Saariyah, including Umar's explanation of the vision behind it and Ali's defence of Umar.
notes: Three narrations are joined: Abdullaah bin Umar, another narration on Ali's reply, and a third on Umar's intention.

summary: Amr bin Haarith reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asked Umar why he made the call, Umar explained the danger his army faced near a mountain, and Saariyah's letter confirmed the Muslims' victory after they turned to it.
notes: Saariyah's letter is quoted in the text.

summary: Asked why he made the call, Umar replied that he said only what Allaah placed on his tongue.
notes: Short follow-up to n03552; the question asked is not stated and the asker is unnamed.

summary: Izzah bint Aas reports that Abu Qirsaafah, whose son had been taken captive by the Romans, would climb a wall at each prayer time and call 'Salaah', and his son heard him from Roman territory.

people.name: Izzah bint Aas bin Abu Qirsaafah

notes: The son is unnamed. Abu Qirsaafah is not matched to the approved abu-quhaafa, which is a different name.

summary: Ibn Abbaas and Aa'isha report that after the Prophet's death, an unidentified voice told the people to bathe his body in his garments, and they did so.
notes: Two reports joined (Ibn Abbaas; Aa'isha). The voice is unidentified.

summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that during a naval expedition led by Abu Moosa Ash'ari, under the Prophet's appointment, a voice from above promised that whoever stays thirsty for Allaah on a hot day will be given drink on the Day of Qiyaamah.
notes: The voice is unidentified.

summary: Abu Burdah reports Abu Moosa Ash'ari's account of hearing a voice at sea promise that whoever fasts on a hot day solely for Allaah's pleasure will be given drink on Qiyaamah, and that Abu Moosa afterwards sought out the hottest days to fast.
notes: The voice is unidentified.

summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that at the funeral of Ibn Abbaas in Taa'if a white bird entered his shroud, and that unseen voices recited Surah Fajr beside the grave.
notes: The reciter is unidentified.

summary: Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that after the sand was levelled over the grave, an unidentified voice was heard.
notes: Short companion report to n03558. The deceased is not named in this item.

summary: Another account adds that a white bird entered Ibn Abbaas's shroud, and Ikrimah explained it as the eyesight the Prophet had promised would return to him at death, and that the verses recited at the grave were heard by all present.
notes: The narrator of this account is not named in the item.
